sources.title: Greenhouse gas reporting conversion factors 2026
facts: DESNZ publishes 2026 full and flat-file conversion factors plus methodology and major-changes material for calculating emissions from activity data.
A conversion factor is a calculation input and is not a directly observed parcel emission value.

sources.title: Conversion factors 2026 voluntary Code of Practice compliance statement
facts: DESNZ states the factors are primarily based on the NAEI and describes peer review, QA and annual improvement processes.
The page explicitly says the factors are a calculation tool rather than statistics themselves.

sources.title: UK government conversion factors for company reporting collection
facts: The collection links annual UK government conversion factors and states they calculate Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions from activity data.
Annual factor editions must retain scheme year and method context rather than being mixed across years.

sources.title: UK ETS country-specific factor list
facts: DESNZ published 2026 carbon emission factors and calorific values extracted from the UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory for UK ETS monitoring.
The factors may only be used where the approved installation monitoring plan and applicable tier rules permit them.

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime how to comply
facts: Environment Agency guidance requires in-scope maritime operators to monitor CO2, CH4 and N2O, verify annual reports and surrender allowances; the first scheme year is 1 July to 31 December 2026.
Maritime operator and voyage-level regulated emissions do not establish emissions for a cadastral land parcel.

sources.title: Download industrial emissions and waste transfer UK PRTR data
facts: Defra publishes the 2024 UK Pollutant Release and Transfer Register dataset as an annual industrial emissions and waste-transfer dataset.
Facility reporting records releases and transfers; they require facility and medium semantics and are not automatically parcel totals.

sources.title: UK Pollutant Release and Transfer Register data sets guidance
facts: Defra explains that facilities report pollutant releases to air, water and soil and off-site waste or wastewater transfers, with operator data subject to regulatory quality checks.
PRTR method codes distinguish measured, calculated, estimated and unspecified values and must remain visible in interpretation.

sources.title: Merchant Shipping MRV carbon dioxide emissions revocation regulations 2026
facts: DfT published the 2026 instrument revoking the previous UK maritime MRV instruments as the new UK ETS maritime regime is introduced.
Revocation or legal transition metadata must not be interpreted as a physical emissions observation.

sources.title: UK ETS scope expansion maritime sector consultation
facts: The UK ETS Authority consultation record documents the July 2026 maritime launch, vessel scope and MRV responsibilities.
Consultation and policy decisions define regulatory scope but do not themselves measure emissions.

sources.title: UK ETS domestic maritime main Authority response accessible webpage
facts: The Authority response confirms the first maritime scheme year and annual report and allowance-surrender timing, including initial double-surrender arrangements.
Compliance deadlines and surrender rules must remain separate from monitored physical greenhouse-gas quantities.

sources.title: MGN 662 United Kingdom MRV regime
facts: Maritime and Coastguard Agency guidance provides templates and technical rules for the earlier UK MRV monitoring plans, emissions reports and compliance documents.
Legacy MRV material must be versioned against the 2026 UK ETS maritime transition and not treated as the current scheme without transition checks.

sources.title: Withdrawn MIN 669 amendment 1 UK MRV parent
facts: The withdrawn notice records the move from the prior UK MRV regime to the UK ETS maritime digital system in 2026.
Withdrawn guidance is retained only for historical and transition provenance and cannot override current UK ETS maritime guidance.

sources.title: Withdrawn MIN 669 amendment 1 UK MRV detailed page
facts: The detailed page states the previous MRV instruments were revoked in April 2026 and provides transitional verification context for emissions data collected before that change.
Historical verification obligations must not be mixed with the new UK ETS scheme-year reporting boundary.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions greenhouse gases by industry and gas dataset
facts: ONS publishes residence-basis CO2, CH4, N2O, HFC, PFC, SF6, NF3 and total GHG emissions by SIC industry through 2024.
Residence-basis industry aggregates are not territorial cadastral-parcel emissions.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions greenhouse gases current edition
facts: The current-edition page exposes scheduled revisions and a March 2026 correction to affected 2023 carbon dioxide values before the June 2026 edition.
A correction must remain distinguishable from a scheduled methodological or data revision.

sources.title: ONS atmospheric emissions greenhouse gases provisional edition
facts: ONS identifies the provisional edition as top-level estimates and documents why planned revisions occur.
Provisional estimates must not silently replace current detailed data or be presented as final parcel observations.

sources.title: ONS greenhouse gas emissions intensity by industry dataset
facts: ONS publishes greenhouse-gas emissions intensity by industry alongside current and provisional editions.
An emissions intensity ratio requires its economic-output denominator and is not an absolute emissions mass.

sources.title: ONS greenhouse gas emissions intensity current edition
facts: The current-edition page documents scheduled revisions and March 2026 corrections affecting several industry intensity tables.
Corrected intensity values remain aggregate industry ratios and cannot be assigned to a land parcel without supported activity and denominator data.

sources.title: NAEI greenhouse gas emissions data hub
facts: NAEI lists the 2026 UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory 1990-2024 and 2026 source pivot table, alongside selectors, point-source, gridded and local-authority products.
National, source, point, grid and local-authority products have different spatial semantics and are not interchangeable with parcels.

sources.title: NAEI emissions factors data selector
facts: The NAEI selector provides UK emission factors by year, pollutant, source, sector, category and fuel where factor-based methods apply.
Missing factors can reflect non-factor methodology or confidentiality, so absence must not be filled with invented values.

sources.title: 2026 post-implementation review of SECR regulations 2018
facts: DESNZ reviews whether SECR has improved transparency and consistency in organisational energy and carbon reporting and considers future simplification.
A policy review assesses reporting effectiveness and is not a physical emissions measurement dataset.

sources.title: SECR regulations evaluation
facts: The DESNZ evaluation uses business surveys, interviews, meter-data analysis, Companies House accounts and cost-benefit analysis.
Evaluation evidence about reporting behaviour or energy use must not be promoted to parcel greenhouse-gas observations.

sources.title: RPC opinion on SECR post-implementation review
facts: The Regulatory Policy Committee describes SECR as a mandatory disclosure framework for large UK businesses and publishes its quality opinion on the PIR evidence.
A regulatory quality opinion does not validate individual company emissions values.

sources.title: RPC opinion SECR PIR detailed page
facts: The detailed RPC opinion records a fit-for-purpose rating and recommends refinements to guidance, consistency and reporting alignment.
Framework quality and reporting consistency remain distinct from direct emissions measurement.

sources.title: Sustainability Reporting Guidance 2025-26
facts: HM Treasury guidance defines minimum public-sector Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting and a materiality approach for Scope 3, with SECR alignment where applicable.
Scope classifications and disclosure requirements must not be confused with territorial parcel-emissions measurements.

sources.title: Environmental reporting guidelines including SECR requirements
facts: Government guidance explains company and LLP energy and greenhouse-gas disclosure requirements and voluntary environmental reporting methods.
Corporate reporting boundaries and intensity ratios require explicit organisational scope and cannot be mapped automatically to parcels.
